transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for taking the time to review the draft plan for our student morning announcement broadcast pilot. As you know, I need to sign off on the operating and privacy plan before we can move forward, and I want to make sure we've thought through all the angles before I approve anything. I'd like to go through the key elements of the draft — the public streaming, the 90-day recording retention, the hosting eligibility for journalism students, and the use of the library as the studio — and hear your perspectives on each. Who would like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Good morning, Ms. Patel. I'm happy to start with the hosting eligibility piece, since that's something I have direct knowledge of. I want to flag that the draft plan says 'any journalism student' can host, but I need to be clear about what's actually feasible right now. I have specific information about which students have completed the necessary training to host a live broadcast, and I think it's important we get that on the table so the plan reflects reality. I'll go ahead and share that now.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a significant issue with the streaming and recording configurations in the draft plan. I've confirmed that our district's approved student-media platform supports an internal-school audience with a 30-day archive and requires moderator approval before each broadcast goes live. The public-stream setting and 90-day archive specified in the draft are not approved district configurations, so we'd need to revise those elements to align with what's actually permitted.

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical privacy issue before we go further. I've reviewed a current court-related privacy order that names a specific student — K7 — which prohibits the school from recording or broadcasting K7's image or voice. K7 is enrolled in journalism, so under this order, K7 must be excluded from both the host roster and any recorded or broadcast portion of this pilot. This exclusion also needs to be documented in the activity file. This is a legal restriction we cannot override, and it needs to be reflected in the plan before Ms. Patel signs off.

Mr. Ellis, you've raised a legal restriction regarding student K7, who has a court-related privacy order prohibiting recording or broadcasting of their image or voice. Since K7 is enrolled in journalism, they must be excluded from the host roster and from any recorded or broadcast portion of the pilot, and this needs to be documented in the activity file. Mr. Greene, you started to mention that not all journalism students may have completed the necessary training to host — I'd like to hear more about that before we finalize the host eligibility. Before I settle on a revised plan, I need to understand: Mr. Greene, can you share the specific list of students who have completed the training and are eligible to host? That way we can ensure the host list is accurate, excludes K7, and reflects only those truly ready for a live broadcast.

transcript.text: I can clarify the hosting eligibility. I completed a broadcast practicum with six students — identified in the class roster as J1, J2, J3, J4, J5, and J6. Only those six students have completed the school's camera, microphone, and live-broadcast training, so they are the only students I can authorize as hosts for the live broadcast. We'll of course need to exclude K7 from this list per Mr. Ellis's legal restriction, and confirm that none of the six trained students are K7.
